name: Astrid Sonne
label: Escho
lede: A viola prodigy who quit the conservatory track at 18, taught herself Ableton by trial and error, and ended up with the year's No. 9 album singing her own songs.

eras.title: Christmas trees and a viola
eras.text: Sonne grew up on the Danish island of Bornholm, where her family runs a Christmas tree business, and started viola at six. She moved to Copenhagen at 16 for classical training, then walked away from it at 18.

years.h: Born on Bornholm, handed a viola at six
years.p: Astrid Sonne grew up on the Danish island of Bornholm, sang in a church as a teenager and played viola from age six.
years.xp: Dazed reports that her family runs a Christmas tree business on the island, and that she worked as a church singer through her teens before heading to Copenhagen. Fact adds that she trained rigorously on viola from the start.

years.h: She quits classical training at 18 and opens Ableton
years.p: Sonne left a strict pre-conservatory programme, then taught herself Ableton Live by trial and error. She told Fact she skipped the tutorials: "I didn't want any help."
years.xp:
She had moved to Copenhagen at 16. Explaining the break, she told Fact she couldn't express what she wanted within the classical track, and that once she found out she could make music herself, she began experimenting.

An early spark was the politically charged electronic music of the Danish producer HVAD. Laurel Halo and Steve Reich came later as reference points. She went on to graduate from Copenhagen's Rhythmic Music Conservatory, per Dazed.

eras.title: Human Lines to Cliodynamics
eras.text: Sonne debuted on the Copenhagen label Escho, a home for the city's experimental scene, and built a catalogue where live viola fights with synthesizers. Danish critics noticed fast.

years.h: Human Lines: viola, choir samples, dubstep synths
years.p: Her debut album on Escho set live viola against choral samples and dubstep-style synthesis. Fact rated her a daring new experimenter.
The EP arrived after the singles "Area Under a Curve" and "Strong, Calm, Slow." Crack covered the latter in September 2019.

years.h: Danish critics crown her Composer of the Year
years.p: Sonne won the Steppeulven Danish Music Critic Prize for Composer of the Year, and won it again in 2022, per her own site.
years.xp: Her site also lists a special mention at the Nordic Music Prize in 2022. In 2020 she appeared on the compilation Kulør 006, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Outside of your lifetime
eras.text: The second album widened the circle: guitar, organ, voices, and friends from the Copenhagen scene. It put her on the international radar.

years.h: outside of your lifetime brings in [[ML Buch|e0f9a19e-a929-4a9f-a5dc-82b2d305f03d]] and an organ
years.p: Ten short tracks mixing synthesizers, strings, drones and choral harmony, with ML Buch on guitar and vocals, Minais B on organ and Tobias Kropp singing, per Boomkat.
years.xp:
Pitchfork put the album in its "Great Records You May Have Missed" for autumn 2021, and both Pitchfork and Paste named it among the year's best electronic records, per Wikipedia.

Boomkat's description points to sequencers tied to esoteric algorithms, fugues in flux and free jazz. It is her last record before she starts writing songs.

years.h: Ephemeral Camera Feed EP lands on Pitchfork's mid-year list
years.p: Pitchfork reviewed the EP in April and placed it on its best albums of 2022 so far that June.

eras.title: Great Doubt
eras.text: After years of instrumentals, Sonne sang her own songs, from a new base in London. The record that came out of it turned a Copenhagen experimentalist into a year-end-list regular.

years.h: A radio set from The Lot in Brooklyn
years.p: Astrid Sonne played The Lot Radio on 26 March 2023, ten months before Great Doubt, a snapshot of the live set as it turned toward song.

years.src: Album of the Year · Dazed · The Vinyl Factory
years.h: Great Doubt: Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and ranked it No. 9
years.p: Her first album of proper songs, with her own voice over viola, woodwinds and harp loops, went to No. 9 on Pitchfork's year-end 50. Escho released it.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne scored the album 77 out of 100, per Album of the Year, which also lists The Guardian at 80, No. 3 at The Vinyl Factory and No. 4 at Resident Advisor. Pitchfork's summary said she turns toward singer-songwriter introspection, finding drama and yearning in understated arrangements.

Dazed described staccato sequencers and jagged structures under gentle vocals. She told The Vinyl Factory that music made "out of duty" wasn't her best work, and that a more relaxed approach followed that realisation.

years.h: "Boost" comes from a bed, not a club
years.p: Sonne told Stereogum she made the single "Boost" lying in bed, an energetic track from a not very energetic place.
years.xp: She described it as capturing a sense of release and of not caring too much, which she said can help when seeking out new settings. Stereogum ran the single as the lead-in to the January 26 album.

years.cap: Sonne and ML Buch on tour, March 2024
years.h: Two Copenhagen friends tour the UK together
years.p: Sonne and [[ML Buch|e0f9a19e-a929-4a9f-a5dc-82b2d305f03d]] shared a UK run in March 2024, including Glasgow's Flying Duck, each supporting a new record: Great Doubt and Suntub.
years.xp:
Talkhouse caught them on the phone before the tour. Buch had urged Sonne years earlier to try songwriting, which she first resisted. Sonne called releasing her first proper songs "really daunting," and enjoyed hearing audiences sing her lyrics for the first time.

Both had left Copenhagen for room to work: Sonne to London, Buch to three years in the countryside.

eras.title: Edits, Coined and the church at Big Ears
eras.text: Friends rebuilt the album, a new duo appeared, and Sonne took a stripped-down string band across North America.

years.h: Coined: a duo with Fine Glindvad
years.p: Sonne and Fine Glindvad formed Coined. Their song "Your House" got pickups from The Face and Paper that month.

years.h: Great Doubt EDITS: Blood Orange, Smerz, HVAD and more
years.p: Sonne asked Blood Orange, ML Buch, Smerz, HVAD, Valentina Magaletti and Lolina for "edits" rather than remixes.
years.xp:
She told Clash the word was chosen so the artists would feel as free as possible with the material. The set includes an off-kilter duet with Blood Orange, a sustained dubplate loop by HVAD and an orchestral introduction by ML Buch.

A video for "Staying here," assembled from fan footage of her summer shows, came out the same day.

years.h: She plays a Knoxville church with violin and cello
years.p: At Big Ears, Sonne played Knoxville's First Presbyterian Sanctuary with violinist Magdalena McLean and cellist Emma Barnaby, working a mixer with close to 100 mappings.
years.xp:
She told The Fader she uses strings to break the wall between performer and audience that laptop sets create. She had played Brooklyn days earlier and said going "full-on crazy" in the church wouldn't have fitted the vibe.

On the pop attention that followed Great Doubt, she said she is adapting to the expectation. Next on her list were more Coined work with Glindvad and work with producer Loraine James.
